name: Enrique Mateo Cobo
headline: From graph paper to machines that move, print and ship.
intro: I design and build things end to end: mechanics, electronics, firmware and software. Most of my projects start as a pencil sketch and end as something running on my desk, or live on the App Store.

sketch.alt: Hand-drawn sketch of the CoreXY printer on graph paper
sketch.label: Sketch · graph paper

built.alt: The finished KMI 2.0 CoreXY 3D printer on an aluminium frame
built.label: KMI 2.0 · built and printing

process.text: Pencil on graph paper, before any software.
Every part modelled in Fusion 360 and checked against the real hardware.
Printed, cut, wired. Often on the machine I'm replacing.
Run it until it breaks, then find out why.
The printed frame flexed, so v2 moved to aluminium extrusion.

principles.title: Constraints as a feature
principles.text: The printer had a hard €120 budget. I recycled the mainboard from my old Creality and only bought what I truly needed: rails, belts, extrusions, endstops.

principles.title: Full stack, both worlds
principles.text: As comfortable with kinematics, steppers and G-code as with React Native, Node and a production backend with real users.
